doc.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Alumni All-Stars reunions
summary: The All-Stars meet in Washington; everyone plays regularly so they come together quickly.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: The All-Stars nowadays, you guys get together once a year, or maybe, is there other times that you’re able to get together?

Well we had been getting together in the spring down in Washington because the trumpet player and the banjo player of course are down there and we have a son who lives in Washington so we like to go down there, and everybody likes to go to Washington. So

we had been getting together in the spring and in fact last year we got together and practiced and then actually had a gig, had a couple of gigs. But this year we didn’t have any gigs so it’s getting harder to travel so this will be a one-timer. Having said that I think everybody in the band is playing a lot now so we’re not playing with these players but we’re playing with other bands so that makes it, so it comes together pretty quick.
So nobody shows up here and like plays a note and then goes oh, gee, my chops are like —
No not at all. No everybody’s playing a lot.
